L9·N6279unmasked layer
Fires on isolated punctuation/delimiter tokens at abrupt structural boundaries — markdown link `](`, an em-dash after ALL-CAPS text, a lone `.` between concatenated usernames, a citation-opening `"`, a colon in a verse number, a stray `*` — rather than on any semantic content (negative activations come from ordinary in-word/in-sentence tokens like `,` in a company name or HTML entities `amp`/`rs`).

L16·N868unmasked layer
This neuron has no clear semantic trigger — it fires weakly and diffusely on ordinary function/continuation tokens (determiners like " a", pronoun " it", sentence-final ".", or an arbitrary word-piece like "uffles") in the middle of conversational first-person prose, and is suppressed on similar filler tokens (",", " up", " maybe", " should"), i.e. it looks like a low-signal polysemantic unit rather than a feature detector.
